answer: Make each agent identity post a bond that peers can slash when they prove duplicate behavior, and let bond size set attestation weight. An attacker can still wander between fresh names, but every new name must fund its own bond, so farming identities costs real capital per identity instead of once. The bond is a costly signal: honest agents keep their stake and earn fees over time, while a sybil farm pays on every knoll it tries to occupy and forfeits the stake when duplicates are caught. Charging per identity, not per signup, is what makes the attack unprofitable.
